description: A supervise function runs a supervisor loop with a hard budget cap, closed roster guard, and idempotency check for repeated calls. Its refused-stop rule requires check_times to pass before accepting a stop action.
source: draft: omp free model + edit: codex

steps.description: The ROSTER defines three sub-agents (extractor, writer, polisher) mapped to their prompts, the only agents the supervisor may call.
The naive_supervisor is a scripted stand-in that always sequences through extractor, writer, polisher, then stops with the newest result whether or not it passed the check.
The mistake: it stops with results[-1] (the polisher output) even if check_times fails, which the real supervisor must not do.
The supervise function initializes transcript, seen set, and facts. The best() helper returns the newest text that passed the check.
best() filters transcript for entries with check == 'ok' and returns the last one, ensuring we only return verified text.

The main loop runs up to budget turns. Each turn calls the decide function (supervisor) and parses JSON. It handles four stop conditions: malformed JSON, stop with check passed, stop refused by check, unknown agent, repeated call, and budget exhausted.

steps.answer: the stop is refused, an error is logged, and the loop continues to the next turn
steps.question: What happens when the supervisor says stop but check_times finds missing facts?

steps.description: Lines 32-37: on stop action, check_times runs; if missing facts exist, the stop is refused with an error appended to transcript and the loop continues.

The supervisor runs: extractor extracts facts, writer drafts (check ok), and polisher changes Thursday to Friday (check fails). The supervisor tries to stop 3 times (all refused). The budget exhausts at 6 turns, returning the draft that passed the check.

title: Supervisor Loop with Budget, Roster, and Four Stop Conditions
